messages.author: e1c430550f86b1f6
messages.subject: Mixture of correlated normal distrubutions
parts:
HI all,

A quick question on mixture model:

Consider y1, y1 as a bivariate normal distribution, if I want to create a finite mixture of the 2 with x1 and w2, would it be possible in STAN?

Many thanks,

Andy

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixture of correlated normal distrubutions
parts:
Yes, you can do a mixture of any two densities
you can express in Stan. But I didn't understand
what you were mixing --- if you could write the density out,
we can show you how to code it.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixture of correlated normal distrubutions
parts:
Hi Bob,

I'm considering the following:

Following the example of the mixture model in the manual (ch 9.3)

If I want to replace with the 2 normal distributions (normal(-1, 2), normal (3, 1)) with a bivariate normal distribution:
[y1, y2] ~ multi_normal ([mu1, mu2], Sigma)

where mu1, mu2 and Sigma are known

How should I do the increment_log_prob statement?

Many thanks,
Andy

There is no y[1] and y[2] in that example, just a single
y!

The generative story is that you choose the mixture component,
then generate the item using that component's parameters.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixture of correlated normal distrubutions
parts:
I'm going to take a guess that he meant the outcomes
as opposed to means or variances, since he said known covariance
and the example had fixed parameters for the normals.

If you have these marginals

y[1] ~ normal(-1, 2);

y[2] ~ normal(3, 1);

and know correlation is rho, then if

Sigma = | 2 rho |
| rho 1 |

mu = | -1 |
| 3 |

you want

y ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);

- Bob
